summary: The study focuses on the structural properties of SnO2 thin films deposited by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) and their application in gas sensor structures. The films were grown on various substrates, and their microstructures were analyzed using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). The research highlights the importance of substrate choice and growth conditions in determining the crystalline orientation and microstructural characteristics of the SnO2 films.
evidence: SnO2 films can be grown by all the usual deposition techniques, e.g. reactive r.f. sputtering, spray pyrolysis, evaporation, and chemical vapor deposition (CVD). More recently, it has been demonstrated that SnO2 thin films applicable to sensor structures can be grown by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE). ALE is a surface-chemistry controlled, CVD-type process for thin films which is frequently applied for the production of oxides.
